chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man: if the thief's hand is taken, is it better to leave it or raise it (amputate it)? He said: Indeed, Safwan ibn Umayyah was reclining in the mosque on his cloak, then he stood up to urinate. He returned and his hand had been taken. He sought his companion and found him, and brought him to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He said: 'Cut his hand.' Safwan said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I forgive that to him.' The Messenger of Allah said: 'Why was that not done before he was brought to me?' And I asked him about forgiveness regarding the fixed punishments before they are brought to the Imam, and he said: 'It is good.'
ai.seo_question: Can the victim forgive a thief before the case is brought to the Imam for hudud punishment?
ai.summary: This hadith from al--Istibsar clarifies the juristic distinction between private forgiveness (afw) and the public right of the Imam in hudud cases, using the precedent of Safwan ibn Umayyah. It establishes that while a victim may forgive before the case reaches the authority, once the matter is formally presented to the Imam, the punishment becomes a right of God and the authority cannot simply waive it based on the victim's prior forgiveness, emphasizing the transition from private right to public divine decree.
